questions.q: Why is a checkpoint that only asks "proceed? y/n" worse than having no checkpoint at all?
options: It costs more in API tokens than any other design
It trains the reviewer to click yes without reading, creating the illusion of oversight without the substance of it
The Claude API rejects tool_result blocks sent after a yes/no prompt
It is technically impossible to implement
questions.explain: A vague confirmation prompt gives a reviewer nothing to actually evaluate, so they rubber-stamp it — which looks like oversight happened when it didn't.

questions.q: What are the three pieces of information this lesson says a reviewer needs to make a real approval decision?
options: The agent's full conversation history, the model name, and the API latency
The exact tool name and arguments, why the agent is doing this, and what concretely happens if they approve
Only the tool's name — the arguments can be inferred
A screenshot of the agent's internal reasoning tokens
questions.explain: Exact arguments (not a paraphrase), the reasoning or goal behind the call, and the concrete effect of approval are what let a reviewer judge the action rather than just click a button.

questions.q: In the real tool_result format, how does a rejected action differ from an approved one?
options: A rejected action uses a completely different content block type called tool_reject
Both use the same tool_use_id in a tool_result block; a rejection sets is_error: true with the reason in content and the tool is never actually called
A rejected action is simply omitted from the conversation entirely
Rejections can only be communicated through the system prompt
questions.explain: Approval and rejection are both tool_result blocks for the same tool_use_id — the difference is that on rejection the real tool never runs, and is_error: true with an explanatory content string tells Claude the action didn't happen and why.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend persisting a pending approval request and stopping the loop, rather than blocking synchronously while waiting for a human?
options: Synchronous blocking is not supported by any programming language
A process that blocks waiting on a human response is fragile and expensive to keep running; a durable, resumable queue is what makes this workable in production
Persisting requests is required by the Claude API's terms of service
It has no practical benefit over synchronous blocking
questions.explain: Humans can take minutes or hours to respond; keeping a process alive and blocked the whole time doesn't scale. Persisting the pending request lets the loop resume later once a decision is made.

questions.q: If a human rejects a delete_customer_record call because the ID looks malformed, what should the tool_result content and is_error field reflect?
options: content should be empty and is_error should be false, since the agent made no technical error
content should explain the reviewer declined and why (malformed ID), and is_error should be true, since the requested action did not happen
The tool_use_id should be changed to a new random value
No tool_result should be sent at all in this case
questions.explain: A rejection is not an application bug, but from Claude's perspective the action didn't succeed — is_error: true with a clear explanation in content is the correct signal so the model can adjust its next step instead of assuming the delete happened.
